interface.title: CosmΩracle (CosmOracle) — cosmological distance calculator
interface.stage_of_work: Quick calculation and exploration before or during analysis: converting a redshift into distances, volumes and times under a chosen cosmology, and producing tables and plots to use elsewhere
interface.what_it_is_for: Enter a redshift and a cosmology (preset or custom H0, Ωm, ΩΛ, Ωr, w0, wa) to get the comoving, transverse comoving, luminosity and angular-diameter distances, comoving volume, lookback time and the physical size of 1 arcsec at that redshift; plot these from z=0 to that redshift; and download the plots as PDF and the data table as a text file.

data.note: There is no data to load. Everything is computed from parameters typed into the sidebar. Three built-in parameter presets fill the fields: Planck-2018 (H0=67, Ωm=0.32, ΩΛ=0.68), WMAP-2012 (70, 0.28, 0.72) and 737 (70, 0.3, 0.7). The exported table (planck_z1.txt, closed_w0wa_z3.txt) is comma-separated even though it is named .txt. Its header is z, DCz [Mpc], DMz [Mpc], DLz [Mpc], DAz [Mpc], VCz [Gpc^3], tlz [Gyr], and it has about 300 rows evenly spaced from z=0 to the chosen redshift. A plot download saves plot.pdf.

tree.specific: Compute cosmological distance measures, comoving volume, lookback time and the 1-arcsec physical scale at redshift z for a chosen cosmology, plot them against redshift, and export the table

features.name: Preset-or-custom model parameter panel with live recompute
features.general: Pick a named reference parameter set that fills a column of numeric fields, change any field by hand, and every result below updates when you press Enter
features.specific: Parameter set dropdown (Planck-2018 / WMAP-2012 / 737) refills H0, Matter Density and Dark Energy Density. Radiation Density, w0, wa, Redshift and Significant Digits (decimal places) are typed text fields, and pressing Enter reruns the Results
steps: Choose a preset from the Parameter set dropdown
Overwrite any parameter field (e.g. ΩΛ to set curvature, w0/wa for evolving dark energy)
Type the target redshift and press Enter
Set Significant Digits to control the decimals shown
Read the recomputed Results block
serves_tasks: Start from a published reference parameter set
Enter custom model parameters, including curvature and evolving dark energy
Get the four distance measures to the target

features.name: Single-point results readout with derived angular scale
features.general: Show, in sentences with units, every computed quantity at one chosen input value, including a derived conversion from angle to physical size
features.specific: Results block lists Dc, Dm, Dl, Da (Mpc), the kpc size of a 1-arcsec object, comoving volume (Gpc³) and lookback time (Gyrs) at the entered redshift, rounded to the chosen number of digits
steps: Enter the redshift
Read the four distances
Read the physical size subtended by 1 arcsec
Read comoving volume and lookback time
serves_tasks: Get the four distance measures to the target
Get the lookback time and enclosed volume out to the target
Convert an angular size to a physical size at the target

features.name: Per-quantity chart with its own log toggle, size sliders and PDF export
features.general: Tick which series to draw against the input range; each chart gets its own log-axis toggle, width and height sliders and a download-as-figure button. The same chart component is reused for an overlay of related series and for less-used quantities kept in a collapsible section
features.specific: Plot Dc(z)/Dm(z)/Dl(z)/Da(z) checkboxes draw one overlay chart from z=0 to the chosen z with distinct line styles and a legend; 'Click for more plots' holds Plot Comoving Volume Vc(z) and Plot Lookback Time tl(z), each as its own chart. Every chart has 'Switch to semi-log scale', plot width/height sliders (1–25) that reshape the matplotlib figure, and 'Download plot' (plot.pdf)
steps: Tick one or more distance checkboxes, or open 'Click for more plots' and tick Vc(z) and/or tl(z)
Optionally tick that chart's Switch to semi-log scale
Adjust that chart's width / height sliders
Press that chart's Download plot to save the PDF
serves_tasks: Overlay chosen distance measures on one chart to see where they diverge, then adjust and save the chart
Plot volume and elapsed time against the same range

features.name: Named export of the computed table
features.general: Type a file name and download the whole computed table (all quantities on a grid of input values) as a delimited text file
features.specific: 'Name the file' text field plus 'Click to download' saves a comma-separated .txt with columns z, DCz, DMz, DLz, DAz [Mpc], VCz [Gpc^3], tlz [Gyr] on about 300 redshifts from 0 to z
steps: Type a file name in Name the file
Press Enter and wait for the rerun to finish
Press Click to download
Open the file for further analysis
serves_tasks: Export the full table of computed quantities against redshift to a named file

features.name: Built-in definitions page with rendered formulas
features.general: A reference page inside the tool that defines each computed quantity and shows its formula, so users can see exactly what is being calculated
features.specific: Documentation page ('Definitions of quantities') renders redshift (1+z=1/a), the Hubble constant, E(z), the D_L and D_A relations and the lookback time integral t_L=H0^-1∫dz'/((1+z')E(z'))
steps: Click Documentation in the sidebar
Scroll through 'Definitions of quantities'
Read the rendered formula for the quantity in question
serves_tasks: Look up the definition and formula of each computed quantity

screens_never_reached: The file names the code notes give ('Cosmological distances', 'Definitions') are shown in this build as 'Distances' and 'Documentation'. Both were visited, so no view was left unreached.
not_done: Opened only the distance-plot PDF (plot.pdf) as a download; it is binary, so its contents were not checked. The Download plot buttons for the Vc(z) and tl(z) plots were not pressed in the main run (the replay pressed tl(z)'s and got another plot.pdf).
Did not try semi-log on the Comoving Volume plot (I tried semi-log on the distance and lookback-time plots).
There is no control for the plot range: plots and the exported table always run from z=0 to the entered redshift, so the 'over a redshift range' comparison is limited to [0, z].

Bad input is not validated: typing 'abc' in Redshift and pressing Enter shows a raw Python 'ValueError: could not convert string to float' traceback (screens/031.webp). Typing 3 again recovers the Results but the plot checkboxes are cleared (screens/032.webp). I did not test edge values such as negative redshift or very high z (e.g. 1100).

Export quirk: pressing Click to download right after typing a new name, before the rerun finished, saved the old name (filename.txt). A second press after the rerun gave the new name. The file is comma-separated even though it is named .txt.

Opened the Dl(z) plot fullscreen via the expand icon and closed it with Escape (screens/034.webp, screens/035.webp); this is Streamlit's generic chart chrome, not part of the tool, so it is left out of the tree and features.
